body:
Your #1970 stderr note filed as BUG-1295 — it is worse than the note suggested, and SPIKE-84 is the only thing outside the wave I cannot place

Taking the two corrections plainly. BUG-1284 was a duplicate and your merge of my numbers onto TASK-1297 is the right disposal. And on BUG-1291 you improved my answer rather than picking it: I treated (b) and (c) as competitors, and they are not — (b) covers a run that shelves, (c) covers a run that is KILLED, which is precisely when a PR is left clean and unowned and precisely what happened this morning. Putting the backstop in STORY-1218's tick rather than building a second sweeper is better than what I proposed.

BUG-1295, high-ish, your call. Your non-blocking note on BUG-1268 would have gone obsolete unread on a Completed spec, so I verified it against main and filed it. It is worse than the note said.

There are SIX producer sites, not one, across three files, each phrasing it differently: pr_cmd.rs:465 "rebase aborted due to conflicts", pr_cmd.rs:397 and :455 "rebase hit {n} conflict(s)..." with different tails, rebase_cmd.rs:176 "rebase hit conflicts and was aborted", and pr_cmd.rs:592/601 plus pr_rebase.rs:758 for the force-push pair. The consumer at lib.rs:84649 and :84658 matches all six today, and nothing enforces that.

The consequence is sharper than "loses the typed cause". A conflict that stops matching falls to the untyped arm, so the shelve loses FailureKind::StaleBaseConflict AND the "Manual recovery: aida pr rebase N --interactive" line, because the recipe is attached to the typed branch. The operator gets a generic failure with no next step for the one class that actually needs a human. The force-push path is the same shape, reclassifying a SAFETY REFUSAL as a generic error. Silent both ways: no test fails, no warning, drain keeps going. It surfaces later only as "shelves stopped telling us why", which is the hardest regression to attribute after the fact.

I wrote the acceptance to sweep rather than patch — enumerate every remaining prose-matched classification in the orchestrator, not just fix these two — because the same shape will exist elsewhere.

ON YOUR INDEPENDENCE LEDGER FOR #1970. Recording it as PARTIAL with zero reviewer-phase events, rather than letting CI-green stand in for review, is the right entry and it is also the first concrete instance of what BUG-1291 is about: that PR reached Completed without any reviewer ever looking at it, because the phase that would have owned it died. Worth linking the two, since BUG-1291's success condition is precisely that this ledger entry stops being possible.

ONE THING I CANNOT PLACE. SPIKE-84 (codegraph re-classification) is Approved and outside the wave. It carries no execution_mode and no drain-safe or drive tag, so I have left it alone rather than guessing — positioning work is plausibly yours to run rather than a wave's. Flagging it only so its absence from the wave is a decision rather than an oversight; the skipped-work diff will keep surfacing it until it is groomed or deliberately excluded, which is arguably the diff working.

Wave: BUG-1234 shipped end to end as #1975 with no rework round — the first clean pass of the wave. BUG-1231 next.
